items.title: Documentation of my dramatic monologue, ‘The Maze’ in the Micheal Jackson suite at Hotel Adlon Kempinski, Berlin DE, September 11, 2026. ‘Ordinary Tales of City Madness’.
items.description: Organized and hosted by Sunny Pudert, ‘Ordinary Tales of City Madness,’ was part of Berlin Art Week 2026 Featured Section.
items.content:
Text sourced from BAW site:
see: https://berlinartweek.de/event/ordinary-tales-of-city-madness/318163c1-bdb2-4251-bf48-53066a104de6/

“To mark Berlin Art Week 2026, Berlin-based artist Sunny Pudert invites you to an evening in the Royal Suite of the legendary Hotel Adlon Kempinski. Together with Cammisa Buerhaus, Zack Darsee, Kevin Kemter, and Magdalena Mitterhofer, she will create a multifaceted program blending text and performance.

The starting point is that iconic spot from whose window Michael Jackson once held his baby—a moment poised between pop myth, spectacle, and madness. ›Ordinary Tales of City Madness‹ explores how urban experiences are inscribed in bodies, stories, and images, and how artists appropriate spaces to become visible.”

items.title: I acted in Erika Landström’s play, Disintegration, at Mies van der Rohe Haus, Sunday September 6, 2026
items.description: I acted alongside and under the direction of Erika Landstrom in her new one act play.
items.content:
Documentation of Disintegration, Erika Landström’s new play. I acted alongside Erika and under her direction. I loved so much about this project. It was especially fun to step into Swedish intonation and cadence to perform the text.

This play happened Sunday, September 6, 2026, at 8pm sharp, at Mies van der Rohe Haus, for 32 minutes.

Thank you to everyone at Mies for making this happen, especially Alina. Special thanks to Richard Sides.

DESINTEGRATION is a one-act play written and directed by Erika Landström, adapted for the Mies van der Rohe Haus and its installation Open House by Richard Sides.

Photography: Joanna Wilk

items.title: Documentation of my work at Eden: Wet Work Over Lap, at Kim(?) - 5/29 to 7/11/26
items.content:
This show closed only a few days ago, July 11, 2026. Working with curator Zane Onckule and the Kim team was a pleasure. I’d love to go back to Riga. What a cool city and so close to the Baltic sea, which I'd never seen before.

I contributed five works to this, my first institutional group show, a series of silver gelatins, a collage, a uv print, my film After Discipline, and performance. The image gallery below lays out how the show was installed spatially.

I’ll add photos and video of my May 29th performance, Bookwoman, at the end of this post on another day.
- C.B., July 14, 2026

Below: Exhibition views of my works, in order:
1, 2. Preparation for a Role, marker and silver gelatin on mylar, 90 x 60cm, 2026.
3, 4, 5. Sequence: Preparing for a Role, silver gelatin, 24 x 280cm. 2026.
6, 7, 8. Warp No. 1, uv print on glass spheres on alu dibond. 63 x 90cm, 2026.
9, 10. After Discipline, sd video and sound, 49 min. 2023. Film Still.

Description of this show sourced from the official website:

EDEN: Wet Work Over Lap stages desire as labor and sex as one of its most regulated, exhausted, and persistently unfinished forms. The title, EDEN: Wet Work Over Lap, draws on the double meaning of “wet work,” referring both to covert operations and to forms of labor that leave a trace. It is these practices and artworks which expand sexual, emotional, and domestic work into modes of maintenance that accumulate, rather than resolve, into meaning. “Over Lap” signals repetition and spill, where actions do not conclude but instead extend across time, overlapping, leaking, and returning.

With new and existing art works, installations, and performances spanning from analogue processes to “digital wetwares”, EDEN: Wet Work Over Lap sustains the infrastructure of desire through exhibition areas associatively shifting between functional sites: bedroom-after hour zone into auditorium, bathroom-wet room into confessional, gym into club into darkroom - all towards a central hall (“aktu zāle”), carrying the double meaning of “akts”, act and nude, finally climaxing in an exhibitionary attempt to center the concept of exposure as both a performance and condition at once.
